hypothesis: Every declared standard path has a reference end state accurate far beyond the integrators under test: closed forms on constant-curvature charts and a 34-digit extrapolated integration on the saddle, torus and gaussian bump.
input_data: Standard paths: plane (L=2.0), sphere (L=2.0), cylinder (L=3.0), saddle (L=1.5), torus (L=3.0), gaussian-bump (L=2.5), hyperbolic-plane (L=1.5), plane-polar (L=2.0), cylinder-polar (L=2.0)
Start states are the binary64 states used by the ciw integrators, converted exactly
mathematical_model: Great circle X(s) = cos(s/R) X0 + R sin(s/R) T0; helix and polar lines through the flat development; hyperbolic semicircles; transfer matrices cn_K, sn_K; otherwise the sympy-derived geodesic + Jacobi system integrated by Gragg-Bulirsch-Stoer in mpmath.
numerical_result: Largest ciw-vs-reference gap 6.38e-14; variable-curvature references saddle mpmath (self-estimate 1.44e-24), torus mpmath (self-estimate 4.35e-23), gaussian-bump mpmath (self-estimate 6.39e-22); Clairaut drift of the ciw end state 6.75e-14.
observation_model: Euclidean distance of embedded end points (chart distance on the hyperbolic plane) and max-abs difference of the 2x2 transfer matrix.
